lesson.title: The Relation Between the Chords of a Circle and its Center

items.quote: The relation between the chords of a circle and its center
items.text: The relation between the chords of a circle and its center

items.quote: What you'll learn
items.text: Deducing the relation between the chords of a circle and its center. How to solve problems related to the relation between the chords of a circle and its center.

items.quote: Equal chords.
Congruent circles
In the figure opposite : A is a point on circle M

items.quote: What is the relation between the length of the chord
items.text: What is the relation between the length of the chord and its distance from the center of the circle?

items.text: If the chords are equal in length, what can you conclude?

items.quote: The distance of chords AE, from the center of circle M equal M X
items.text: Notice that: The distance of chord AE from the center of circle M equals MX where X is the midpoint of the chord AE, in circle M which its radius length is r.

items.quote: The closer the chord is from the center of the circle, the longer
items.claim: The closer the chord is from the center of the circle, the longer its length is and vice versa.

items.quote: If chords of a circle are equal in length, then thay are equidistant from the center.
items.claim: Theorem: If chords of a circle are equal in length, then they are equidistant from the center.

items.quote: Theorem diagram with points C, A, Y, X, D, B, M
items.caption: Circle with centre M; chords AB and CD with perpendiculars MX to AB (X on AB) and MY to CD (Y on CD), right angles marked at X and Y; dashed segments MA and MC drawn. Points C, A, Y, X, D, B, M labelled.

items.quote: Given: AB = CD, MX ⊥ AB, MY ⊥ CD
items.text: Given: $AB = CD$, $\overline{MX} \perp \overline{AB}$, $\overline{MY} \perp \overline{CD}$. R.T.P.: Prove that $MX = MY$. Construction: Draw $\overline{MA}$, $\overline{MC}$.

items.quote: Proof: ∵ MX ⊥ AB ∴ AX = 1/2 AB
items.text: Proof: ∵ $\overline{MX}\perp\overline{AB}$ ∴ $AX=\frac{1}{2}AB$. ∵ $\overline{MY}\perp\overline{CD}$ ∴ $CY=\frac{1}{2}CD$. ∵ $AB=CD$ ∴ $AX=CY$. ∵ the two triangles AXM and CYM both have: $AM=CM$; $m(\angle AXM)=m(\angle CYM)=90^\circ$; $AX=CY$ (Proof). ∴ $\triangle AXM \equiv \triangle CYM$. We get: $MX=MY$ (Q.E.D.)
items.notes: Proof printed as a theorem proof, recorded as one block.

items.quote: In congruent circles, chords which are equal in length, are equidistant from the centers
items.claim: Corollary: In congruent circles, chords which are equal in length are equidistant from the centers.

items.quote: are two equal chords in length in circle M and X is
items.stem: $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{AC}$ are two equal chords in length in circle M and X is the midpoint of $\overline{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{MX}$ intersects the circle at D, $\overrightarrow{MY} \perp \overline{AC}$ intersects it at Y and intersects the circle at E. Prove that: First: $XD = YE$. Second: $m(\angle YXB) = m(\angle XYC)$.
solution: Given: $AB = AC$, X is the midpoint of $\overline{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{MY} \perp \overline{AC}$
R.T.P.: First: $XD = YE$; Second: $m(\angle YXB) = m(\angle XYC)$
Proof: since X is the midpoint of $\overline{AB}$, therefore $\overrightarrow{MX} \perp \overline{AB}$
since $MD = ME = r$, therefore $MD - MX = ME - MY$, therefore $XD = YE$ (Q.E.D 1)
in $\triangle MXY$: since $MX = MY$, therefore $m(\angle YXM) = m(\angle XYM)$ (1)
From (1) and (2) we get: $m(\angle YXB) = m(\angle XYC)$ (Q.E.D 2)

items.stem: Two concentric circles M, $\overline{AB}$ is a chord in the larger circle and intersects the smaller circle at C and D, $\overline{AE}$ is a chord in the larger circle and intersects the smaller circle at Z and L. If $m(\angle ABE) = m(\angle AEB)$, then prove that: $CD = ZL$.
solution: Proof: In $\triangle ABC$: $\because m(\angle ABE) = m(\angle AEB)$ $\therefore AB = AE$.
In the larger circle: $AB = AE$ (proof) $\therefore MX = MY$ (theorem)

learning_objectives.label: Chord length versus distance
learning_objectives.description: Compare the lengths of chords of a circle with their distances from the center, using >, < and =, and find the range of a value from such a comparison.

learning_objectives.label: Equal chords are equidistant
learning_objectives.description: Use the theorem that equal chords are equidistant from the center (also in congruent circles) to find lengths and angles and to prove equalities.

learning_objectives.label: Converse: equidistant chords are equal
learning_objectives.description: Use the converse of the theorem, that chords equidistant from the center(s) are equal in length, to calculate chord lengths and prove chords equal, including in concentric and intersecting circles.
